/-!
# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)

The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
  Σ-component of the universal element.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/

/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat

      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
    intro i j Z gi gj hg
    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
    exact hs i
  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
      (ht' i)
    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem

/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

end AlgebraicGeometry

20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.

14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
74	-/

92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.

100	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
101	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
102	    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),

104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113	
114	This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
115	expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility
116	that is not needed. -/
117	lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
118	    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
119	    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
120	  rfl

126	coverage for the restricted family.

129	witness's image in the chart source lies inside `V i`.  Everything else is the lift along the
130	open immersion `(V i).ι` and `restrictChart_app_apply`, which is `rfl` — so this direction
131	carries no mathematics beyond the lift, and together with its converse below it is a
132	biconditional rather than a reduction.  **It closes no gate.**

135	opens or all witnesses.  So a producer discharges it exactly where it produces the witness,
136	which is the only place the information is available; a formulation asking for the containment
137	uniformly over all witnesses would be strictly stronger.

139	What the containment *means* geometrically depends on which open `V i` is, and this file
140	deliberately does not assume an answer — in particular `V i` is an open of the chart source
141	while `chartLocus` is a set on a test, so the two are not interchangeable and the intended
142	instantiation still owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge (cost: `haff`, i.e. dat-b's B-4). -/
143	theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
145	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
146	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
147	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
148	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
149	    PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
150	  intro T s t
151	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
152	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
153	  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
154	  exact hx

157	/-- **The composite**: coverage plus the containment gives the local-surjectivity instance
158	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
159	`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
160	is built from.

162	Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
163	owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
164	theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
165	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
166	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
167	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
168	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
169	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
170	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
171	      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
172	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)
173	
174	/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra
175	
176	A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
177	naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
178	together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/

180	variable (C) in
181	/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
182	pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.
183	
184	So `liftPointwiseToOpens`' hypothesis is not a strengthening chosen to make the proof go: it
185	is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the

189	The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
190	and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by
191	`restrictChart_app_apply`. -/
192	theorem pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
193	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
194	    (h : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
195	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
196	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
197	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
198	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base) := by
199	  intro T s t
200	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, u, hu⟩ := h T s t
201	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, u ≫ (V i).ι, hu, ?_⟩
202	  intro z hz
203	  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := hz
204	  exact ⟨u.base w, rfl⟩

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: the coverage obligation is Zariski-local in the test, so AFFINE tests suffice
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduced `ChartsCoverLocally` — and with it
12	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to pointwise data at **every test scheme
13	`T`**.  That is where the reduction chain stops, and the quantifier it stops at is the
14	problem this file addresses.
15	
16	**Every divisor-side producer in this project is indexed by a RING, not by a scheme.**
17	`DivFamZar C S π n` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`) is a quotient of local-equation
18	systems over an algebra `S`; `divFamZar C π n T` at a general test
19	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`) is the affine-opens *limit* of those, and the
20	comparison `divFamZarAffineEquiv` (:300) collapses it to `DivFamZar` only on an affine
21	test.  Likewise every producer of a certified family, of an effective witness
22	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`), and every classifier
23	(`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`, :217) is stated over a ring or a field.  So a coverage
24	lane facing "for every scheme `T`" has to cross the affine-to-general gap **before** it can
25	use any of that machinery, and nothing said it was allowed to skip it.
26	
27	It is allowed to skip it, and that is this file's content.
28	
29	## Why locality in the test is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
30	
31	The naive argument — "sieves are local, so restrict to an affine cover" — is not available
32	as stated, because `ChartsCoverLocally` is a statement about the sieve on `T` itself, and
33	the pointwise hypothesis quantifies over points of `T`.  Three things have to be checked,
34	and each is where the argument could fail:
35	
36	* **the class must restrict.**  The datum at a point `t` of an affine piece `Y` is about a
37	  section over an open of `Y`, while the obligation at `t : ↥T` is about an open of `T`.
38	  Composing `W.ι ≫ 𝒰.f j` gives a map into `T` but not an *open of* `T`, so the transport
39	  cannot be done at the level of `T.Opens` — it has to be done at the level of the sieve,
40	  where an arbitrary morphism is allowed;
41	* **the sieve must be transitive.**  Membership of `⨆ i, imageSieve (f i) s` in the
42	  topology on `T` is deduced from membership of its *pullbacks* along the cover maps, which
43	  is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` plus `Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve` — the latter is
44	  what says the pullback of an image sieve is the image sieve of the restricted section,
45	  i.e. that the obligation at `Y` is about `s|_Y` and nothing else;
46	* **the pullback must commute with the supremum.**  `Sieve.pullback` is a left adjoint on
47	  sieves, so it preserves `iSup`; without that the per-piece obligations would be about a
48	  different sieve than the one the pullback of the target names.
49	
50	None of the three mentions `pic⁰`, a chart, or a divisor.  That is the point: the
51	affine-to-general passage for antecedent 2 is a fact about the site, and mixing it with the
52	geometry is what made it look like part of the geometry's price.
53	
54	## What this does and does not buy
55	
56	It buys the quantifier, and only the quantifier.  `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` below
57	asks for the pointwise datum **only over affine schemes**, and produces
58	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test; `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` composes that
59	with B-6.  So a producer may now assume its test is `Spec S` and reach for
60	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj`, `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` and the rest
61	of the ring-indexed machinery directly.
62	
63	It does **not** produce the datum at an affine test.  That is B-5's geometry and it remains
64	open; per `Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` and the `dat-b` row the residue there is
65	the class-side question, and per `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` the range containment `hV` is
66	a further separate obligation.  What changes is that the residue is now stated where the
67	tree's producers live.
68	
69	**On the converse, corrected.**  An earlier version of this paragraph said
70	`affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` makes the affine and general forms "equivalent", and cited
71	that as discharging the `reduction-needs-its-converse` safeguard.  It does not: that
72	declaration is `rfl`-equal to `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally`, its `[IsAffine Y]` binder is
73	never used, and the direction it certifies is the *free* one — general pointwise data gives the
74	affine data by `fun Y _ s y => h Y s y`.  So the affine form is a genuine **weakening** of the
75	general one, which is exactly why `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` is worth having; the
76	honest certificate is that theorem, not a no-op converse (audit `I-1023`).  The converse is
77	kept only as the affine-test instance of the pointwise extraction, which is what it is.
78	
79	**On the atlas, and this is the sharper limit.**  Nothing here pins `V`.  The statements below
80	take an arbitrary family `f`, which is what makes the site content reusable — but a consumer
81	must supply coverage at the *same* `V` at which antecedent 1 was certified, and `ajcr-p1`
82	measured both ends of that range to be bad: `hf` is free at `V = ⊥` (`isChartUniv_bot`, with a
83	construction that never mentions the Abel chart), while `V = ⊤` returns the unrestricted
84	certificate that three headers call false.  So any workable `V` is a proper intermediate open,
85	CHART-U(b)'s openness is load-bearing, and the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` has **no measured
86	inhabitant at any `V`** (`I-1012`).  Two bad endpoints are two refutations, not a non-vacuity
87	check.
88	
89	## Main declarations
90	
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine` — **the site fact**, with no
92	  presheaf and no chart: a sieve on `T` is covering as soon as its pullback along every map
93	  from an affine scheme in a cover of `T` is covering.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` — **the reduction**: pointwise
95	  coverage over affine tests only gives `ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` — the composite with B-6, i.e.
97	  the instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test data alone.
98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the converse, so the affine form
99	  is not a strengthening.
100	-/

111	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

117	/-! ## The site fact -/
118	
119	/-- **A sieve is covering as soon as it is covering after pullback to affine pieces.**
120	
121	Stated for an arbitrary sieve on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses.  The
122	cover is `Scheme.affineCover`, whose members are affine by
123	`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`, and the deduction is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive`
124	against the presieve the cover generates.
125	
126	This is the step the coverage chain was missing: it says the Zariski-local-surjectivity
127	obligation may be discharged one affine piece of the test at a time. -/
128	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
129	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
130	      Scheme.zariskiTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
131	    S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
132	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
133	      ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T :=
134	    Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
135	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
136	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
137	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
138	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)

140	/-! ## The reduction -/

142	variable (C) in
143	/-- **THE AFFINE-TEST REDUCTION**: pointwise coverage over affine tests gives
144	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
145	
146	The hypothesis is `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`'s, with `[IsAffine Y]` added and
147	nothing else changed.  So a coverage producer may assume its test is affine — hence, through
148	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, that its divisor data lives over a *ring*, which is where every
149	producer in this project is stated. -/
150	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
151	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
152	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
153	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
154	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
155	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
156	  intro T s
157	  refine mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine _ fun j => ?_
158	  -- the pullback of the supremum is the supremum of the pullbacks, and each is the image
159	  -- sieve of the RESTRICTED section — so the obligation at the affine piece is exactly the
160	  -- affine instance of the hypothesis
161	  have hpb : (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s).pullback (T.affineCover.f j)
162	      = ⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i)
163	          ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s) := by
164	    -- `Sieve.pullback` preserves `iSup` (it is a left adjoint), and per index it turns the
165	    -- image sieve of `s` into that of `s` restricted along the cover map
166	    simp only [← Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
167	    ext Y g
168	    simp only [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply, Sieve.pullback_apply]
169	    aesop
170	  rw [hpb]
171	  -- the piece is affine (`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`), so the hypothesis applies AT IT — note
172	  -- `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` cannot be cited here, since it quantifies over all tests
173	  -- and would demand the datum at the non-affine ones too; the site bridge is what is reused
174	  choose W hW i x hx using h (T.affineCover.X j)
175	    ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s)
176	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun y => ⟨x y, hx y⟩
177	
178	variable (C) in
179	/-- **B-5 over affine tests ⟹ B-6**: the local-surjectivity instance
180	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test coverage data alone. -/
181	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
182	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
183	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),

28	*membership of the locus* needs.

9	/-!
10	# B-5 step 3: `b = n` IS FORCED, AND IT IS THE CALIBRATION, NOT A DEFECT (I-0660 adjudicated)
11	
12	A reviewer (I-0660) measured that `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`
13	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean:134`) has a hypothesis pack that **forces `b = g`**, and
14	concluded that its `hb` "cannot be DAT-0a's threshold" and that step 3 is therefore not
15	"derived".  **The arithmetic is right; the conclusion is one step too strong, and this file
16	settles which parts stand.**
17	
18	## What is confirmed, and it is a real correction to this lane's prose
19	
20	`ledger_forces_b_eq_n` reproduces the reviewer's derivation and generalises it: at a chart index
21	legal at parameter `n` — i.e. satisfying the constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − n` that
22	`chartValueTrans` / `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:382`) require — the
23	hypothesis `hdeg` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` **determines `b`**, and `b = n`.  So
24	`b` is *not* a free parameter that DAT-0a may instantiate: the chart index pins it.
25	
26	`hb_forces_h0_eq_one` then shows what `hb` at `b = n` amounts to on a genus-`g` curve at `n = g`:
27	**every** degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`.  That is false on any curve with a degree-`g`
28	effective divisor moving in a positive-dimensional family, and it is strictly stronger than
29	every threshold theorem in the tree (DAT-0a's bound is `n₁·deg F + 1 − χ = n₁·deg F + g` with
30	`0 < deg F`, so it exceeds `g` as soon as `n₁ ≥ 1`).  The reviewer's reading of the *strength*
31	is therefore confirmed, and sharpened: it is not merely "stronger than a threshold result", it
32	is a statement the χ-ledger converts into an `h⁰` equality for every divisor at once.
33	
34	## What does NOT follow — and this is the correction to the reviewer
35	
36	The reviewer's conclusion assumes `n = g`.  **`n` is a free parameter of the entire chart
37	layer.**  `divFunctor C π n`, `chartValue C π n m Z`, `chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg` and
38	`abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg` are all stated for an arbitrary `n : ℕ`; nothing in
39	`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` or `DivSchemeAbel.lean` pins it.  `n = g` is where the *divisor
40	representability lane* instantiates (`divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause`,
41	`DivRepAffPullClause.lean:475`), and where `Pic^0` has the right dimension — but the coverage
42	theorem does not know that.
43	
44	So `b = n` is a **calibration equation between two independently chosen numbers**, and reading
45	it as "an over-constraint" versus "the definition of the chart parameter" depends entirely on
46	which of `n` and `b` is free.  `index_of_threshold` records the direction that is actually
47	available: given DAT-0a's threshold `b ≥ 0` at the splitting field, a chart index constraint at
48	parameter `b.toNat` makes `hdeg` hold **by construction**.  There is no obstruction to
49	satisfying `hdeg`; the obstruction is that satisfying it *at n = g* requires the sharp
50	vanishing.
51	
52	## THE HONEST STATUS OF STEP 3, therefore
53	
54	Three statements, all now machine-checked, none of which was the one the roadmap carried:
55	
56	1. `hdeg` is satisfiable, for every threshold `b ≥ 0`, at the chart parameter `n := b.toNat`
57	   (`index_of_threshold`).  So coverage-at-a-chart-index is not blocked.
58	2. At the *representability* parameter `n = g`, `hdeg` forces `b = g`, and `hb` at `b = g` is
59	   the sharp vanishing — **not available, and not expected to be true**
60	   (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`).
61	3. Hence the residue is neither "instantiate DAT-0a" (the roadmap's claim, too optimistic) nor
62	   "restate with slack" (the reviewer's repair, which as they themselves note runs into the
63	   `0 ≤ Σ` legality of the index).  It is: **reconcile the chart parameter with the threshold.**
64	   The chart family the atlas glues may be indexed by `m`, and `d₁ = classDeg k Θ > 0`, so the
65	   available move is to let the chart index *at parameter g* carry the slack in `Z` rather than
66	   in `n` — which is exactly `classDeg_presenting_twist_eq_add`'s `g + e` shape, whose own
67	   legality (`0 ≤ Σ`) is the open question.
68	
69	That is a genuinely different residue from the one the roadmap and the reviewer each named, and
70	it is recorded here rather than in prose only.
71	
72	## Main declarations
73	
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ledger_forces_b_eq_n` — the reviewer's derivation, at general `n`.
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.index_of_threshold` — the converse: every nonneg threshold is realised as

theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (x : Y ⟶ D.left) :
    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) x
      = ⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :=
  rfl

/-! ## The `haff` residue, named

`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.

For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance
hypothesis that used to sit beside it was discharged
(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.

Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))

variable (C) in
/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.

Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff

/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.

For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting

/-!
# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.

## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible

A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
leaving it to unfold at a use site.

What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.

## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline

`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:

> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three

**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.

**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.

So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
named so it cannot be lost again.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
-/

## What this file closes

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece

> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
> nothing here produces such a datum.

**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
it they are the same class.

## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction

`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.

automatic:

* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
